keyTakeaways: Whether you need a photo depends on your visa and its checklist.
Many checklists ask for a recent passport-sized photo, 35 mm wide x 45 mm high.
The photo should be no more than 6 months old, on a plain background.
There is no single official file size or pixel size for every visa upload.
Follow the limits shown on your checklist and upload screen.
intro: **Quick answer:** Many Australian visa checklists ask for a recent passport-sized photo (45 x 35 mm, which is 35 mm wide x 45 mm high), no more than 6 months old, on a plain background. Digital limits depend on your visa and the upload screen, so follow the numbers shown in your ImmiAccount or on your checklist.
**[Check my photo with the Australian passport photo checker →](/australian-passport-photo-checker)**
This page explains what the checklists ask for, why websites give conflicting file sizes, and how to prepare a photo that fits your own application.

sections.heading: Do you need a photo for an Australian visa?

subsections.heading: Which visa checklists ask for a photo
content: Some Australian visa checklists ask for a photo and some do not. It depends on the visa you are applying for and how you apply.
Do not assume every visa needs one. Your checklist is the only reliable answer.

subsections.heading: How to find your own checklist
content: Start on the [Department of Home Affairs website](https://immi.homeaffairs.gov.au/) and open the page for your visa. Look for its document checklist.
If you apply online, the ImmiAccount upload screen also shows what it accepts. If you apply through an embassy or visa application centre, use the checklist it gives you.

subsections.heading: Why requirements depend on the visa
content: Each visa has its own checklist, and some checklists are older than others. The photo rules can differ between them.
That is why one page online cannot give you a single rule for every Australian visa.

sections.heading: What size is an Australian visa photo?

subsections.heading: Printed visa photo: 45 x 35 mm in many checklists
content: Many embassy and visa checklists ask for a recent passport-sized photo of 45 x 35 mm. Written width first, that is 35 mm wide x 45 mm high.
If your checklist gives a different size, follow your checklist.

subsections.heading: Size in cm and inches
content:
| Unit | Width x height |
|---|---|
| Millimetres | 35 x 45 mm |
| Centimetres | 3.5 x 4.5 cm |
| Inches | 1.38 x 1.77 in |
To convert, divide millimetres by 10 for centimetres, or by 25.4 for inches. For example, 35 ÷ 25.4 = 1.38 inches.

subsections.heading: Why you should not trust one-size-fits-all numbers online
content: Websites quote different file limits for Australian visa photos, such as 50-500 KB, 70 KB-3.5 MB or 1 MB. We could not find an official Home Affairs source that sets one limit for all visa uploads.
So we do not give you a number to copy. Use the one on your own upload screen or checklist.

sections.heading: What are the digital upload requirements?

subsections.heading: Where the exact limits are shown
content: The upload screen and checklist for your visa show the exact limits. Follow those.
Read the screen before you prepare your file, so you know the file type and size it accepts.

subsections.heading: Format: JPEG is the usual choice
content: JPEG is the most widely used photo format, and it is the format Home Affairs asks for in citizenship applications. Confirm that your visa upload screen accepts it before you save your file.
Phones sometimes save photos in other formats, such as HEIC. Convert the file if your upload screen does not accept it.

subsections.heading: What Home Affairs publishes for citizenship
content: For citizenship applications, Home Affairs asks for a JPEG between 70 KB and 3.5 MB, with a preferred resolution of 1200 x 1600 pixels. Details are in our [citizenship photo guide](/guides/australian-citizenship-photo-requirements).
That spec is for citizenship. It is a useful guide to the kind of file Home Affairs works with, but it is not a visa rule.

sections.heading: What background, pose and quality do you need?

subsections.heading: Plain light background
content: Checklists ask for a plain background. A plain white or light grey wall, with no pattern or objects, is the safest choice.
Make sure the background contrasts with your face and hair.

subsections.heading: Face centred, eyes open, neutral expression
content: Face the camera straight on, with your face centred, eyes open and a neutral expression. Keep your hair away from your eyes and the edges of your face.
These are the same basics used in the [Australian passport photo requirements](/guides/australian-passport-photo-requirements), which are a good standard to aim for.

subsections.heading: No filters, no scans of photos, no photos of photos
content: Turn off filters and beauty modes. Do not edit your face or replace the background.
Use the original digital photo. Home Affairs does not accept a scan of a photo or a photo of a photo for citizenship, and the same approach is wise for visas.

subsections.heading: Tourist and visitor visa applicants
content: Check the checklist for the exact visitor visa you are applying for. Do not rely on a friend's application from a different year or a different visa.
If a photo is requested, take a new one that is no more than 6 months old.

subsections.heading: Applicants from India
content: Many searches for Australian visa photos come from India. The rules are set by your visa checklist, not by the country you apply from.
If you apply through a visa application centre, follow the checklist it gives you. Indian passport photos are a different size, so do not reuse one without checking.

subsections.heading: Babies and children on a visa application
content: If your checklist asks for a photo of a child, the same basics apply: plain background, face straight on, no other person or object in the frame.
Our [baby passport photo guide](/guides/australian-baby-passport-photo) has tips for photographing young children.

sections.heading: How do you prepare your visa photo?

subsections.heading: Take or choose a clear photo
content: Ask someone to take the photo, or use a professional provider. Stand in front of a plain light wall with even light on your face.
Pick the sharpest photo with your eyes open and a neutral expression.

subsections.heading: Crop and check it with our tool
content: Our [Australian passport photo checker](/australian-passport-photo-checker) checks head height, background, lighting and glasses. It is a useful pre-check for a visa photo.
If you need a 35 x 45 mm digital file, our [Australia visa photo maker](/australia-visa-photo-editor) can crop one for you.

subsections.heading: Check the file against your upload screen
content: Before you submit, compare your file with the limits on your upload screen: file type, file size and any pixel size it shows.
If the screen rejects the file, adjust it to match those limits rather than a number you found online.

subsections.heading: Department of Home Affairs
content:
- [Department of Home Affairs: visas and ImmiAccount](https://immi.homeaffairs.gov.au/)
- [Photo requirements for citizenship applications](https://immi.homeaffairs.gov.au/citizenship/apply-for-citizenship/prepare-application/photo-requirements) (citizenship spec, quoted above as a guide only)

subsections.heading: Your visa checklist
content: The checklist for your visa, and the upload screen in ImmiAccount, are the official sources for your photo limits. They take priority over anything on this page.

subsections.heading: Last updated
content: Last updated: 21 November 2026. We checked these rules against the official pages on this date.
Rules and file limits change, so we review this page every 3 months. Always read the official page on the day you apply.

faq.question: What is the Australia visa photo size?
faq.answer: Many Australian visa checklists ask for a passport-sized photo of 45 x 35 mm, which is 35 mm wide x 45 mm high. The photo should be no more than 6 months old, on a plain background. Your own checklist is the final word, so follow it if it says something different.

faq.question: Can I upload a selfie for an Australian visa?
faq.answer: It is better not to. A selfie is usually taken too close, which distorts your face, and it is hard to keep your head straight. Ask someone to take the photo, or use a professional provider. Then check it against your visa checklist and upload screen.

faq.question: What is the Australia visa photo size in inches?
faq.answer: A 35 x 45 mm photo is about 1.38 inches wide x 1.77 inches high. To convert millimetres to inches, divide by 25.4. In centimetres it is 3.5 x 4.5 cm. Check your visa checklist first, because the required size can differ between visas.

faq.question: Is the visa photo the same as the passport photo?
faq.answer: Not exactly. An Australian passport needs 2 dye-sublimation prints on 200 gsm glossy paper, with set size and head rules. A visa photo follows your visa checklist, and is often a digital upload. The basics, such as a plain background and neutral expression, are similar.

faq.question: How old can my Australian visa photo be?
faq.answer: Checklists we found ask for a photo no more than 6 months old. Use a recent photo that shows how you look now. If your checklist gives a different time limit, follow the checklist, because rules can vary between visas and between older and newer checklists.

faq.question: Does an Australian tourist visa need a photo?
faq.answer: It depends on the visa and how you apply. Some checklists ask for a photo and some do not. Open the checklist for your exact visa on the Home Affairs website, or check the ImmiAccount upload screen, to see whether a photo is requested.
